subject: german
title: Stamp 1: Classical Literature
welcome_lead: Stamp the giants of German literature: Goethe, Schiller, Mann.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on classical and modern German literary heritage.

concepts.def: German polymath (1749-1832), author of Faust and Die Leiden des jungen Werthers.
Goethe's two-part tragedy; Part I (1808), Part II (1832); pact with Mephistopheles.
Playwright (1759-1805), author of Wilhelm Tell and Die Rauber.
Weimar Classicism around 1786-1805, centred on Goethe and Schiller.
Novelist (1875-1955), Nobel Prize 1929, wrote Der Zauberberg and Buddenbrooks.
Storm and Stress; pre-Romantic movement around 1770-85 emphasising emotion.

walkthroughs.body_html: Faust, dissatisfied with knowledge, makes a pact with Mephistopheles. Part I focuses on Gretchen's tragedy; Part II explores cosmic themes. The work is the pinnacle of German literature.
Schiller's plays explore freedom and tyranny. Die Rauber (1781) was a Sturm und Drang sensation; Wilhelm Tell (1804) dramatises Swiss independence struggle.
Thomas Mann won the Nobel Prize in 1929. Buddenbrooks (1901) traces a Hanseatic family's decline. Der Zauberberg (1924) is set in a Davos sanatorium and meditates on European civilisation.
